h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר ו׳ Pesach — Maamar Vav

p: "then we, our children and our children's children
They have already noted the change of language:
and likewise afterward, in the paragraph "Therefore":
"He took us out from slavery to freedom," etc.,
The matter is: a slave is one
acquired with ownership of his body,
by means of a debt he owes.
And this is what we say:
"and Hashem our God took us out" — to freedom.
claims against us, for he pursued us;
that is, because of the prosecution that still existed,
and as they said in the Mechilta
"'And the waters were to them a wall (chomah)'—written deficient;
for there was wrath against Israel as well;
and so it is written in Bereishis Rabbah
שֶׁקִּיטְרֵג הַסָּמֶ"ךְ מֵ"ם: עַד עַכְשָׁיו עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְכוּלֵּי,
that the Satan prosecuted: "Until now [these were] idol worshippers, etc.,"
and likewise in the holy Zohar
וְכֵן בְּשִׁיעְבּוּד מַלְכִיּוֹת יֵשׁ טְעָנוֹת עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And similarly in the subjugation to the kingdoms there are claims against Israel,
וּגְאוּלָּה הַיְינוּ בִּמְחִיר כֶּסֶף, וּמִשִּׁיעְבּוּד צָרִיךְ גְּאוּלָּה,
and "redemption" means with a monetary price, and from subjugation (debt) one needs redemption;
and concerning this it is said
"You were sold for naught, and you shall be redeemed without silver."
וְזֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: מֵעַבְדוּת לְחֵירוּת וּמִשִּׁיעְבּוּד לִגְאוּלָּה.
And this is what we say: "from slavery to freedom, and from subjugation to redemption."
וְזֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: וְאִילּוּ לֹא הוֹצִיא וְכוּלֵּי מְשׁוּעְבָּדִים הָיִינוּ לְפַרְעֹה בְּמִצְרַיִם
And this is what we say: "And had He not brought out, etc., we would have remained subjugated to Pharaoh in Egypt"
וְהַיְינוּ אַף שֶׁמְּדִינַת מִצְרַיִם נֶחֶרְבָה וּפַרְעֹה נֶאֱבַד,
meaning that even if the country of Egypt were destroyed and Pharaoh perished,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מְשׁוּעְבָּדִים הָיִינוּ לִקְלִיפַּת פַּרְעֹה בְּמִצְרַיִם שֶׁהוּא עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ,
nevertheless we would have remained subjugated to the husk of Pharaoh in Egypt, which is "the nakedness of the land,"
וְאַף שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל הָיוּ גְּדוּרִים מִן הָעֲרָיוֹת אָז
and even though Israel were fenced off from immorality then
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא זָכוּ לְהִתְבָּרֵר בְּמִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם, וְהָיָה עוֹד עֲלֵיהֶם קִטְרוּג וְשִׁיעְבּוּד.
nevertheless they had not yet merited to be refined in the attribute of Tzaddik Yesod Olam, so prosecution and subjugation still remained upon them.
וְזֶה שֶׁחָשַׁב "מִיָּגוֹן לְשִׂמְחָה", עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
And this is why it listed "from sorrow to joy," along the lines of what they said
"The upright to joy"—"for the upright of heart, joy."
וְהַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁזּוֹכִין לְשַׁבָּת עִילָּאָה, וְזוֹכִין לְהוֹרִיק הָרַע מִלֵּב כְּסִיל לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ מִכֹּל וָכֹל,
That is, when they merit Supernal Shabbos and merit to completely empty out the evil from "a fool's heart at his left,"
זַכָּאָה מַאן דְּעָבֵיד לוֹן דִּירָה בְּשַׁבָּת בִּתְרֵי בָּתֵּי לִיבָּא, וְאִתְפְּנֵי יֵצֶר הָרָע מִן תַּמָּן
"Fortunate is he who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbos in the two chambers of the heart, and the evil inclination is cleared out from there"
וּ"מֵאֵבֶל לְיוֹם טוֹב" — אוֹר כִּי טוֹב, חָכְמָה, שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד זֶה מַאֲמַר יְהִי אוֹר,
and "from mourning to a festive day (Yom Tov)"—light is "good" (ki tov), which is Chochmah, corresponding to which is the utterance "Let there be light,"
חָמֵשׁ פְּעָמִים אוֹרָה בְּמַאֲמַר יְהִי אוֹר כְּנֶגֶד חֲמִשָּׁה חוּמְשֵׁי תוֹרָה
with five mentions of light in the passage of "Let there be light" corresponding to the Five Books of the Torah
וּ"מֵאֲפֵילָה לְאוֹר גָּדוֹל" — גָּדוֹל מוֹרֶה בְּלֹא שִׁיעוּר יוֹתֵר עַל הַתְּפִיסָה, שֵׂכֶל הַנֶּעְלָם מִכָּל רַעְיוֹן.
and "from deep darkness to great light"—"great" indicates without measure, beyond grasp, the intellect hidden from all thought.
וְשָׁלֹשׁ לְשׁוֹנוֹת הַלָּלוּ כְּנֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת שְׁלֹשָׁה אָבוֹת שֶׁהֵם מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדּוֹת חֶסֶד גְּבוּרָה תִּפְאֶרֶת,
And these three expressions correspond to the holiness of the three Patriarchs, who are chariots for the attributes of Chessed, Gevurah, and Tiferes,
וְהֵם עֲנָפִים מִשָּׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר
and they are branches from the first three Sefiros, as brought in the Zohar
עֲבִיד לְאַבְרָהָם בְּרָזָא דְּחָכְמָה, לְיִצְחָק בְּרָזָא דִּתְבוּנָה, לְיַעֲקֹב בְּרָזָא דְּדַעַת.
"He made Avraham in the secret of Chochmah, Yitzchak in the secret of Tevunah (Binah), and Yaakov in the secret of Da'as."
And this is what is brought in the holy Zohar
ש' רָזָא דִּתְלַת אֲבָהָן וּבַת מִתְעַטְּרָא בְּהוֹן,
"Shin is the secret of the three Patriarchs, and Bas is crowned with them,"
ש' תְּלַת כִּתְרִין: כֶּתֶר חָכְמָה וּבִינָה.
"Shin is three crowns: Kesser, Chochmah, and Binah."
וְאַחַר כָּךְ "וּמִשִּׁיעְבּוּד לִגְאוּלָּה", שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד קְרִיעַת יַם סוּף,
And afterward "and from subjugation to redemption," which corresponds to the Splitting of the Sea,
"I have given Egypt as your ransom,"
שֶׁנִּצְרַךְ לָזֶה כּוֹפֶר וּמְחִיר כְּדֶרֶךְ הַגְּאוּלָּה,
for this required a ransom and a price, as is the way of redemption,
and it is like what they said
וְנָשָׂא הַשָּׂעִיר — זֶה עֵשָׂו, אֶת כָּל עֲוֹנֹתָם — עֲוֹנוֹת תָּם, דִּכְתִיב
"And the goat shall bear—this is Esav—all their iniquities—the iniquities of the wholesome man (tam), as it is written
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיְּבָרֵר ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁעֵשָׂו הוּא הַחַיָּיב בַּעֲוֹנוֹת תָּם
That is, Hashem, may He be blessed, clarifies that Esav is the culpable one for the iniquities of the wholesome man
כֵּן בֵּירֵר ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ אָז בִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף,
so did Hashem, may He be blessed, clarify then at the Splitting of the Sea,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמִצְרַיִם שֶׁהֵם קְלִיפַּת הַתַּאֲוָה, עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ,
that because Israel were in Egypt, which is the husk of lust, "the nakedness of the land,"
עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִכְנַס מְעַט מִזֶּה בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל, שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה,
a trace of this entered the heart of Israel as the leaven in the dough,
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי נִטְבְּעוּ הַמִּצְרִים בַּמַּיִם הַזֵּידוֹנִים וְיִשְׂרָאֵל נִגְאֲלוּ אָז גְּאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה.
and therefore the Egyptians were drowned in the raging waters and Israel were then redeemed with a complete redemption.

paragraphs.text: Mechilta, Beshalach (on Shemos 14:29) — "The ministering angels were astonished: 'Master of all worlds! Idol-worshippers walking on dry land in the midst of the sea!' From where do we know that the sea too was filled with wrath (chemah) against them? Above it is spelled chemah, here chomah." Rav Tzadok reads the defective spelling חמה as wrath against Israel too.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Moshe Teitelbaum, Yismach Moshe, Shemos — “The Midrash says that the very wrath with which the sea was filled against Israel He turned back upon Egypt. Would the Holy One, blessed is He, execute judgment without justice? But it is understood through the Midrash that the angel of Egypt argued, ‘How are these different from those? These are idol worshippers and those are idol worshippers,’ and the Blessed One answered, ‘You judge the coerced like the willing; they worshipped only out of subjugation.’ And it is known what the Shelah said on ‘And the Egyptians made us evil,’ that they made us evil and sinful. Thus the wrath was turned upon Egypt, for they were the cause, and Israel were coerced.” Connection: Yismach Moshe reads the wrath at the sea as Rav Tzadok does, the charge against Israel answered by showing that Egypt put the sin into them; he adds the angel's argument and the Divine reply, that Israel acted under compulsion, which turns the punishment due Israel onto Egypt.

But it is understood through the Midrash that the angel of Egypt argued, ‘How are these different from those? These are idol worshippers and those are idol worshippers,’ and the Blessed One answered, ‘You judge the coerced like the willing; they worshipped only out of subjugation.’ And it is known what the Shelah said on ‘And the Egyptians made us evil,’ that they made us evil and sinful. Thus the wrath was turned upon Egypt, for they were the cause, and Israel were coerced.” Connection: Yismach Moshe reads the wrath at the sea as Rav Tzadok does, the charge against Israel answered by showing that Egypt put the sin into them; he adds the angel's argument and the Divine reply, that Israel acted under compulsion, which turns the punishment due Israel onto Egypt.
